Unfortunately we cannot take on that responsibility, so we'd need an MRP
I understand, and thanks for the responses. 🙏 I'll try again today to produce a minimal repro and will add another comment in the next ~10 hours.

I spent all day investigating this, but unfortunately, I don't think I made any real progress. There are some observations that I made:

- I have a Nintendo Switch Pro controller connected to my computer. I think something is misconfigured about the deadzones since it spams `_Input` functions with `InputEventJoypadMotion` events. Without the controller connected, this issue doesn't repro.
- Seemingly unrelated and innocuous code somehow has an impact on this repro. For example, I have a C# file that is completely unused but is still bundled via the `.csproj` file. Commenting out its contents turns a 100% repro into a 0% repro. Similarly, this happens when I comment out a random `public const float Foo = 0.2f;`. For all I know, the controller issue is a red herring based on this bullet point.

I think I'm at an impasse, and I'm going to give up. Feel free to close this bug.

Okay, this kept eating at me, so I spent another bunch of hours today investigating, and [I have a repro](https://github.com/AdamLearns/TypedExportArrayShutdownCrash). It's as minimal as I could get it; many of the C# files are very basic. I added instructions to the `README`.

There are actually two crashes:

  - 49 of 100 runs crashed due to `handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11`
  - 14 of 100 runs crashed with `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::system_error: mutex lock failed: Invalid argument`

I tried the linked repro on `Windows 11` and `macOS Tahoe 26.5.1`(Macbook M4) but could only get it to crash on mac. It took a while to figure out a decent delay(1.4 - 1.9) that triggers the crash about 1/10 runs on my machine.

Godot versions tested:
- `4.7.beta4.mono.official`
- Compiled from source using a recent master commit `070dc9897ea1b84ab2a7ec04b9bc1b94f38a0eaf` with `dev_build=yes`

The dev build hits this assert as already mentioned by @AdamLearns and after that it crashes inside a dotnet finalizer thread because it tries to access the CSharpLanguage singleton which already has been deallocated at this point and is null.

The script that is trying to get destroyed is the same as reported by Adam `ActionMarkupHandler.cs`.

Assert
```
ERROR: FATAL: DEV_ASSERT failed  "_first == nullptr" is false.
   at: ~List (./core/templates/self_list.h:135)
```

Took a look into `OnGodotShuttingDownImpl` and after some API searching, I think problem might be here. Here is the buggy timeline I GUESS:
- Step1: dotnet runtime GC collected some RefCounted objets, but their finalizer is not called at once.
- Step2: `OnGodotShuttingDownImpl` manually `Dispose()` all "disposable" objects, but objects in Step1 is not included because they are GC collected and their `WeakReference` should be invalid
- Step3:  `DEV_ASSERT(_first == nullptr);`
- Step4: dotnet Finalizer thread finally call Step1 objects' finalizer

So I modified `OnGodotShuttingDownImpl`, manually trigger GC and wait for all finalizer finished at the end of the function, and after that, this problem is not shown yet. (I've tested for about 10 times)
<details>
  <summary>My fix</summary>

```
private static void OnGodotShuttingDownImpl()
{
    bool isStdoutVerbose;

    try
    {
        isStdoutVerbose = OS.IsStdOutVerbose();
    }
    catch (ObjectDisposedException)
    {
        // OS singleton already disposed. Maybe OnUnloading was called twice.
        isStdoutVerbose = false;
    }

    if (isStdoutVerbose)
        GD.Print("Unloading: Disposing tracked instances...");

    // Dispose Godot Objects first, and only then dispose other disposables
    // like StringName, NodePath, Godot.Collections.Array/Dictionary, etc.
    // The Godot Object Dispose() method may need any of the later instances.

    foreach (WeakReference<GodotObject> item in GodotObjectInstances.Keys)
    {
        if (item.TryGetTarget(out GodotObject? self))
            self.Dispose();
    }

    foreach (WeakReference<IDisposable> item in OtherInstances.Keys)
    {
        if (item.TryGetTarget(out IDisposable? self))
            self.Dispose();
    }

    if (isStdoutVerbose)
         GD.Print("Unloading: Finished disposing tracked instances.");
     
    // MY FIX: waiting for all finalizers finished
    GC.Collect(GC.MaxGeneration, GCCollectionMode.Forced);
    GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers(); 
    // MY FIX END
}
```
</details>
